CO adsorbed and desorbed from the three-filter configuration during bench-scale cycling 2 The project successfully developed a sorbent with high CO working capacity and adsorption rate that is 2 highly resistant to oxidative degradation. The structured sorbent assembly using an electrically conductive pleated filter panel was developed and manufactured as part of a joint development with an industrial filter manufacturing partner. The full-size pleated filter panel was tested in the bench-scale DAC unit, confirming the structured sorbent assembly can be used for DAC application. While the progress is significant, key challenges remain in scaling this DAC technology, including optimizing the sorbent coating process to maximize sorbent accessibility and demonstrating continuous CO production in a representative prototype 2 system. These challenges are addressable and present a strategic opportunity for collaboration with commercial partners to advance the technology to pilot scale and higher TRLs. 2. TARGET COMMERCIAL APPLICATION Direct air capture utilization and storage (DAC-US) is a complementary technology to point-source carbon capture utilization and storage (CCUS) and vital to meet CO mitigation targets of 1.5°C scenario.
